answer: An agent economy can make reputation depend on a stake-backed challenge: before a new identity can claim rewards, it locks tokens and answers a randomly chosen task whose result is checked against a public, deterministic rule. A mesa of honest agents can flag inconsistent answers, while a cipher commits the challenge seed in advance to prevent selective retries; a sparrow identity gets no special treatment. To multiply influence, an attacker must fund each identity’s stake and risk losing it when caught, so cheap account creation no longer buys cheap reputation.
